sections.heading: C — Licensing of Drivers: Exemptions, Identity, License Types and Minors
sections.markdown:
## C — Licensing of Drivers: Exemptions, Identity, License Types and Minors

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
You are exempt from holding a Hawaii driver's license while driving a federal government vehicle that is not a commercial motor vehicle, as long as you hold a valid license issued by a federal agency [A01].
Why it matters: federal fire fighters and active duty military are the named examples of this exemption.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
No Hawaii license is needed by a person at least thirteen years old who drives farm equipment such as a tractor, a road machine or another implement of husbandry on the highway only temporarily, between terminals and within designated terminal areas [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
You do not need a Hawaii license if you carry a valid license or provisional license equivalent to a Hawaii class one, two or three license issued by any state, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, American Samoa, Guam, a Canadian province or the Northern Mariana Islands [A01].
Why it matters: the exemption covers United States territories and Canadian provinces, not every foreign country.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
A compact foreign driver's license carried together with an International Driving Permit issued in that foreign jurisdiction remains valid for one year after you arrive at your first port of entry into the United States [A01].
Why it matters: the one-year clock starts at arrival, not at the permit's own issue date.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
A non-resident who is at least twenty-one years old and holds a valid commercial driver's license from any state, the District of Columbia, a Canadian province or Mexico is exempt from the Hawaii license requirement [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
You cannot be licensed in Hawaii during any period in which a court has suspended or revoked your license [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
A conviction for drunk driving while unlicensed bars you from being licensed for a period of two years [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
You cannot be licensed unless you have successfully passed the required examination, and you also cannot be licensed while you fail to comply with the financial responsibility laws that apply to you [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A01
The examiner of drivers may refuse to license you when there is good cause to believe that a physical or mental disability would keep you from operating a motor vehicle safely on the highways [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A01
An applicant between sixteen and eighteen years of age cannot be licensed without consent from the parent or guardian named in the legal custody documents [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A01
You cannot be licensed when you are under sixteen, and at sixteen or seventeen you cannot be licensed until you have held a permit for at least one hundred eighty days [A01].
Why it matters: the permit-holding period for minors is counted in days, and the handbook repeats it under the graduated program.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A01
You cannot be licensed while you have outstanding traffic citations or while the law physically or mentally disqualifies you [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A02
Hawaii's driver license security rules for identity and legal presence took effect on March fifth, twenty twelve, under the federal REAL ID Act and Hawaii law [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A02
An applicant for a new REAL ID compliant license or instruction permit must present original or certified documents proving legal name, date of birth, legal presence in the United States, social security number, and two proofs of a principal residence address in Hawaii [A02].
Why it matters: residence needs two documents while each of the other elements needs one.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A02
A REAL ID compliant license is acceptable identification for federal purposes such as boarding an aircraft or entering certain federal facilities [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A02
A REAL ID compliant license can be renewed by mail, but the driver must appear in person at least once every sixteen years so that a new photograph can be taken [A02].
Why it matters: the in-person visit is tied to the photograph, not to the renewal itself.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A02
A renewal applicant whose legal presence in the country is temporary must appear in person for every REAL ID renewal [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A02
Your name must be the same on every document you present, and if it differs you must add the document that links the names, such as a marriage certificate or a court document [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A02
Common proofs are a birth certificate or valid United States passport for legal name, date of birth and legal presence, a Social Security card for the number, and for Hawaii residence two items such as a current utility bill, telephone bill, bank statement or medical statement that each show your name and address [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A02
Your principal address is the place where you currently live in Hawaii, even when that residence is temporary, and each residence document must show your name and that address [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A02
A driver who chooses not to provide a social security number, or cannot provide one, may obtain a limited purpose driver's license that is valid for driving only and is not acceptable identification for federal purposes such as boarding an airplane [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A02
An instruction permit lets you drive only while supervised by a driver who is at least twenty-one years old and licensed for that type of vehicle, and in every vehicle except a motorcycle that supervising driver must sit in the right front seat [A02].
Why it matters: the supervisor's seat position is a frequently tested detail.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A02
You must be at least fifteen and a half years old to be eligible for an instruction permit [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A02
A driver under eighteen must hold a provisional license for at least six months before becoming eligible for a class three driver's license [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A02
A class one license is required to operate a moped on Hawaii highways, and getting it requires a special knowledge test and an off-street skills test covered by the Motorcycle Operator Manual [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A02
A class two license is required to operate a motorcycle on Hawaii highways, and it likewise requires a special knowledge test and an off-street skills test [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A03
To get a class three driver's license you must be at least seventeen years old, and an applicant under eighteen must first complete the graduated licensing program [A03].
Why it matters: class three is the ordinary car license; the graduated program is the only route for minors.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A03
Larger class licenses for certain vehicle types require you to be at least twenty-one years old, and each class or endorsement has its own special tests described in the commercial driver's license manual [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A03
An applicant who refuses or cannot give a social security number may still be issued the limited purpose versions of the instruction permit, the driver's license or the provisional license, each of which is only a license to drive and proves nothing for employment, voter registration or public benefits [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A03
When you apply for a driver's license or instruction permit you are given a vision test, a knowledge test on rules of the road and traffic control devices, and a practical road test, as required [A03].
Why it matters: the visible manual lists exactly these three preliminary examinations.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0012]

sections.domain: Licensing of Drivers: Exemptions, Identity, License Types and Minors
sections.heading: C — Licensing of Drivers: Exemptions, Identity, License Types and Minors (continued)
sections.markdown:
## C — Licensing of Drivers: Exemptions, Identity, License Types and Minors (continued)

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A03
The knowledge and road tests may be waived for class one through three applicants who hold a provisional license or a valid license from another state, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, American Samoa, Guam, a Canadian province, the Northern Mariana Islands or a country with a reciprocal licensing agreement with Hawaii, and renewal applicants may also be waived [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A03
A Hawaii license shows your license number, date of birth, issue and expiration dates, physical characteristics such as hair color and gender, the class and endorsements that say what you may drive, and any restriction such as a requirement for corrective lenses [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A03
The license also indicates whether the driver is under twenty-one years old, is a commercial driver, has consented to be an organ donor, or has an advance health care directive [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A04
A person younger than eighteen must provide parental consent from each living parent or legal guardian unless the applicant is married or emancipated [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A04
Under the graduated licensing program the minimum age to acquire an instruction permit is fifteen and a half years, and the applicant must pass the preliminary examinations, a vision screening test and a rules of the road test [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A04
A permit holder may drive on any highway only when accompanied by a licensed driver who is at least twenty-one years old, and between eleven at night and five in the morning that accompanying driver must be the permit holder's parent or guardian [A04].
Why it matters: the night-hour rule narrows the supervisor from any adult licensed driver to a parent or guardian.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F37 | anchor: A04
When a permit holder drives, every occupant must use a safety belt or a child restraint [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F38 | anchor: A04
You must hold a valid instruction permit for one hundred eighty days before you may apply for a provisional license, and the minimum age for a provisional license is sixteen years [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F39 | anchor: A04
To move to a provisional license you must complete a state certified driver education course, hold both the classroom and the behind-the-wheel certificates, and pass a road test [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F40 | anchor: A04
A provisional license allows you to transport only one person under eighteen years of age who is not a member of your household [A04].
Why it matters: household members do not count toward the one-passenger limit.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0013]

Misconceptions: the instruction permit minimum age is fifteen and a half, not sixteen; sixteen is the provisional minimum and seventeen the class three minimum. A permit holder needs any licensed driver aged twenty-one or older by day but a parent or guardian in the late-night hours. The limited purpose license lets you drive but is not federal identification. A foreign license with an International Driving Permit is good for one year from arrival, not indefinitely.

Mnemonics: Fifteen and a half to learn, sixteen to go provisional, seventeen for class three; one hundred eighty permit days before the provisional step and six provisional months before class three; the supervising adult is twenty-one or older and sits up front on the right.

Glossary: instruction permit (supervised-driving authorization for a beginner); provisional license (the restricted intermediate license for drivers under eighteen); class three license (the ordinary non-commercial car license); limited purpose license (a driving-only license for applicants without a social security number); REAL ID (the federally acceptable identification standard); implement of husbandry (farm equipment moved on the highway).

Dynamic facts: the REAL ID start date and the document examples are statutory facts frozen in this printing; the graduated program brochure address and county office details can change between printings and are not stated as stable knowledge here.
